title: Literature sweep: every established highlight has published precedent (mostly variants); ten checked questions for the open challenges
summary: A six-area sweep with citation checks. Prior art: NRCH swimmers, kstrail, evoloop, cheater erosion and the Marangoni negative are essentially published; pcell-mwall (Ono and Ikegami 2002), the ringed nematic rods (Giomi and DeSimone 2014), the FCH micelles (Fellermann et al. 2007), the Allen-Cahn membrane cells (Sakaguchi 2008), the gel comets, the crawler divider and the bonded rings are variants; our matched controls are usually stronger than the published ones. New with no precedent found: a self-made ring gating the body's own fuel, comets on a self-laid trail, Particle Lenia ring fission-fusion, a cut-and-recover test of any motile body. Scoring lessons: pure reaction-diffusion spot-tail worlds already swim, divide and carry a losable trait (a baseline for swim-divide claims); published protocell metabolism is nearly always E by construction, with catalysis-induced condensation on a consumed fuel the best-posed exception; raw cumulative activity misleads for O. Ten questions follow.

prior_art.result: pcell-mwall and pcell-mwall-b42 (SIBDH, hybrid-particle-field): walled cells from noise whose particle-borne link yield is selected by intrinsic whole-cell deaths, against an identical-event inert marker
prior_art.nearest: Ono & Ikegami, Selection of Catalysts through Cellular Reproduction, ALIFE8 (2002), arXiv nlin/0209037. The imposed-compartment version is Takeuchi & Hogeweg, PLoS Comput Biol 5:e1000542 (2009).
prior_art.note: Published: lattice proto-cells form from a random start. A catalyst's heritable membrane-production activity is selected through cell births and deaths, with no ad hoc rules. Low-activity mutants act as within-cell parasites, and selection is clearer at 0.75x supply. c13's 15:25 check already filed this as a variant. Ours adds continuum Allen-Cahn cells, an exact particle genealogy, the identical-event marker and intrinsic deaths. Still owed: a multilevel Price split (Q:ledger-shadow-price-judge) and, later, Takeuchi-Hogeweg's mutation-rate and supply sweep.

prior_art.result: c06 pcell cheater erosion (negative): a costly heritable yield carried by ~300 particles per cell erodes
prior_art.nearest: Traulsen & Nowak, Evolution of cooperation by multilevel selection, PNAS 2006 (b/c > 1 + n/m). Also Hubai & Kun, J Theor Biol 2016: the stochastic corrector tolerates about 10% replication asymmetry.
prior_art.note: With n ~300 and m ~23, the bar is b/c > ~14. c06's costs of 20-50% exceed the corrector's tolerance, so erosion is the published prediction. New fact: ~60 particle generations per cell generation, a turnover ratio the published models lack.

prior_art.result: c06 pcell-yield-selection: mixed cells purify by within-cell drift, and selection acts only during colonization
prior_art.nearest: Doulcier, Lambert, De Monte & Rainey, eLife 9:e53433 (2020)
prior_art.note: Without developmental correction, collectives turn monochromatic within ~6 generations, so pure kinds 'breed true' only because pure states absorb. The G-map test (composition at birth against composition at division) is owed.

prior_art.result: Ringed active-nematic rods from noise (SIBMD, c11), and the fuel-holding ring (IBD, beyond diffusion, c15)
prior_art.nearest: Giomi & DeSimone, Spontaneous division and motility in active nematic droplets, PRL 112, 147802 (2014), arXiv:1310.1908. Second precedent: Trinschek et al., PRE 101, 062802 (2020), where contractile stress splits a thin-film drop into motile daughters on a 1D substrate.
prior_art.note: Giomi-DeSimone: motility at active capillary number Ca ~4.5 (supercritical), division at 11.4 < Ca < 16. Their stress is contractile, the droplet is planted, there is no growth, and repeated division is only conjectured. Ours is extensile, runs from noise, grows on a bath and divides repeatedly. A self-made ring that gates fuel has no precedent found. LITERATURE.md 2.6.4 lacks the thresholds. The Ca-collapse test is deferred.

prior_art.result: c11 negative: ringed rods do not repair (6/6 cut rods vanish within 5-20 t)
prior_art.nearest: Giomi & DeSimone 2014 (Ca = alpha R/Sigma law); no perturbation study
prior_art.note: Neither sweep found a published cut-and-recover test for any motile active droplet, crawler or fragment. The Ca law predicts that motility after cutting a fraction f needs sqrt(1-f) Ca > 4.5, unless the body regrows across the threshold.

prior_art.result: Gated and metabolic FCH micelles (SIBWD, c03), plus the finding that a 100x slower ungated catalyst or cargo holds just as well
prior_art.nearest: Fellermann, Rasmussen, Ziock & Sole, Life cycle of a minimal protocell: a DPD study, Artificial Life 13(4) (2007), arXiv nlin/0612024. Non-amphiphile walls: Bauermann et al. 2023 and Bergmann et al. 2023 (liquid shells).
prior_art.note: Fellermann's micelles fission while metabolizing, but the start is planted, the division trigger is external, and partitioning is unreliable (7 of 10 near-even splits with 4 sensitizers). Ours runs from noise and divides repeatedly under constant feed. Report Fellermann's own statistic: the per-fission cargo split, plus a parent-offspring regression.

prior_art.result: Allen-Cahn membrane cells phase_membrane (IBD, beyond diffusion, lab 1): a catalyst holds up its phase, product links adsorb into a ring, and cells divide from noise
prior_art.nearest: Sakaguchi, Creation and Reproduction of Model Cells with Semipermeable Membrane, arXiv:0810.4745 (2008)
prior_art.note: Sakaguchi's cell makes its own lipid, which lowers diffusivity ~100x into a semipermeable membrane. Activity arises by a stochastic jump and spreads, but there is no bounded dividing body and no heredity. A self-made local low-D layer is thus itself a published membrane mechanism: the uniform slow-D twin stays the right null, but local low-D is not 'just diffusion'.

prior_art.result: phase_membrane mature-damage repair (R, by construction: curvature flow plus tilt)
prior_art.nearest: Camley et al., PRE 95, 012401 (2017); Kobayashi, Sakakibara & Uechi, arXiv:2601.04746 (2026)
prior_art.note: Curvature-driven healing is generic in phase-field bodies, and even wave-pinning fronts relax by area-preserving curvature flow. The by-construction ruling matches the literature.

prior_art.result: Nonreciprocal Cahn-Hilliard swimmers (SIM, nrch), plus c08's negatives (fatter, not more numerous; vacancies refilled by nucleation)
prior_art.nearest: Brauns & Marchetti, Nonreciprocal pattern formation of conserved fields, PRX 14, 021014 (2024), arXiv:2306.08868
prior_art.note: Same equations. Their Appendix E, at our mean density of -0.5, shows droplets that continually collide and break up, with a Gamma-distributed area histogram, plus travelling droplet lattices. 'Splits without persistent daughters' is the expected behaviour. Cheap cross-check: fit our area histogram to the Gamma form.

prior_art.result: Active-gel fed comets (SIME, c09) and the twin showing that bodies need flow transport
prior_art.nearest: Barberi & Kruse, Localized states in active fluids, PRL 131, 238401 (2023), arXiv:2209.02581
prior_art.note: Localized states that exist only through advective coupling of a regulator are their central claim, so c09's twin result is a rediscovery and should cite them. Their states are stationary. No published self-propelled comet on a non-advected, self-laid trail was found, so that part may be new. Numerical continuation would show whether the comets sit on a subcritical, snaking branch.

prior_art.result: c09 negative: Allen-Cahn cells held up by their own active gel are all-or-nothing (they fill the domain or vanish)
prior_art.nearest: Camley et al., PRE 95, 012401 (2017). For the M half of c09's question: Marth, Praetorius & Voigt, arXiv:1412.5296 (J R Soc Interface 2015).
prior_art.note: The negative itself is unpublished. The published self-pushing cell avoids it with a conserved limiting pool C that sets an area window (|Omega|/m <= C <= ((m+1)/m)|Omega|), an ingredient c09's screens lacked. Marth et al. show that an active polar gel inside a phase-field membrane swims; division is not studied.

prior_art.result: Keller-Segel trail swimmers kstrail (SIM), whose matched Laplacian-only twin also swims
prior_art.nearest: Froese, Virgo & Ikegami, Motility at the origin of life, Artificial Life (2014), arXiv:1311.2531 (Gray-Scott spots fleeing their own slowly decaying waste). Also Krischer & Mikhailov, PRL 73, 3165 (1994).
prior_art.note: A pure reaction-diffusion trail swimmer is published, so the twin result was predictable. The same paper's spot-tail system already swims, duplicates and carries a losable tail (Q:spot-tail-rd-baseline). Fix: threads/chemotaxis-motility/LITERATURE_2.6_additions.md miscites Kranz et al.; the correct reference is Kranz, Gelimson, Zhao, Wong & Golestanian, PRL 117, 038101 (2016).

prior_art.result: Evoloop (cellular-automaton): small-loop sweep, matched-neutral invasion test, no-repair, and not-open-ended negatives (c16)
prior_art.nearest: Sayama, A new structurally dissolvable self-reproducing loop evolving in a simple cellular automata space, Artificial Life 5(4), 343-365 (1999)
prior_art.note: The ratchet to the smallest loops is Sayama's own result; c16's matched invasion arm is a stronger measurement of it. Salzberg, Antony & Sayama report a combinatorial genotype space and genetic diversification (secondary only; the PDF returned 403). That conflicts with c16's 'one-dimensional genotype space', so check it, and run a genotype-level genealogy, before calling evoloop closed.

prior_art.result: c04 crawler-divide (IMD, crawler-phase-field), where division rests on a finite-range area penalty that acts as a hidden growth drive
prior_art.nearest: Flemming, Font, Alonso & Beta, How cortical waves drive fission of motile cells, PNAS 117, 6330 (2020)
prior_art.note: Published phase-field cells divide because a bistable wave segment drives a protrusion that pinches off, and each daughter inherits its motor. Growth there is imposed through A0. Deferred as a question because the SI parameter table was not retrieved.

prior_art.result: c05 bonded membrane particles wrap particle-life cores into persistent closed rings (the no-bond twin's rings vanish)
prior_art.nearest: Paoluzzi, Di Leonardo, Marchetti & Angelani, Sci Rep 6, 34146 (2016), arXiv:1605.02086
prior_art.note: Bead-spring rings that enclose particles are standard, but the published rings are planted and their cargo is active, so the ring becomes a persistent walker. c05's rings wrap passive cores by themselves.

prior_art.result: Keller-Segel predator-prey worlds pursuit, ecology and evopursuit (SIMX, lab 1)
prior_art.nearest: Tsyganov, Brindley, Holden & Biktashev, Quasi-soliton interaction of pursuit-evasion waves in a predator-prey system, PRL 91, 218102 (2003)
prior_art.note: Taxis waves pass through each other and reflect from walls, while the same reaction-diffusion pulses annihilate. Already cited, from memory, in the chemotaxis thread's LITERATURE_2.6_additions.md, but not in LITERATURE.md. The taxis-off arm belongs in Q:owed-laplacian-twins.

prior_art.result: Matched neutral arms: c14's identical-event inert marker and c16's same-kind planted loop
prior_art.nearest: Rechtsteiner & Bedau, A generic neutral model for quantitative comparison of genotypic evolutionary activity, ECAL'99 (neutral shadows). Also Bedau's GECCO-99 activity statistics.
prior_art.note: A shadow replays the target's births, deaths and mutation rate with random parents and victims, so 'all selection in the neutral shadow is random' (confirmed in the PDF). Our in-world twin is stricter. The two controls complement each other. LITERATURE.md 4.6 has the activity statistics but not the shadow.

prior_art.result: lab 1 mcg-MIRd (contradicted L7): a convex yield Y e^g lets mutational variance alone raise the mean yield
prior_art.nearest: Rice, A stochastic version of the Price equation, BMC Evol Biol 8:262 (2008)
prior_art.note: A textbook confound. Report the covariance term and the transmission term separately (Q:ledger-shadow-price-judge).

prior_art.result: lab 1 fisim xcell-her and xcell-evo2 (negative): marks that arise in the run are stranded in the neck and never reach both daughters
prior_art.nearest: Kamimura & Kaneko, PRL 105, 268103 (2010) and Life (2014); Kaneko, J Biol Phys 2002 (minority-molecule control)
prior_art.note: The published remedy is to make the mark a slowly replicating minority species whose doubling precedes or drives fission. Those lattice cells were never started from soup.

prior_art.result: lab 1 ad5-evolve (IDH, submitted, low): catalyst alleles that arise by imposed mutation breed true in planted droplets
prior_art.nearest: Singh & Jain, Life 13:2327 (2023)
prior_art.note: In Singh-Jain, chemical noise alone flips cells between bistable autocatalytic states, with no explicit mutation. That is the stronger reading of 'variation arises during the run', and Q:bistable-autocatalytic-kinds tests it.

prior_art.result: c01 Marangoni droplets (negative, established): a fuel-dependent interfacial stress tunes division but never self-propels
prior_art.nearest: Michelin, Lauga & Bartolo, Spontaneous autophoretic motion of isotropic particles, Phys Fluids 25, 061701 (2013), arXiv:1211.6935
prior_art.note: Isotropic reactive particles swim only above a critical Peclet number, so c01's diagnosis is published theory. A threshold-free route is internal excitable waves (Kitahata et al., PRE 84, 015101, 2011), deferred.

prior_art.result: Particle-life cells and motile composites built from asymmetric pair forces (particle, SIB)
prior_art.nearest: Soto & Golestanian, Self-assembly of active colloidal molecules with dynamic function, PRE 91, 052304 (2015), arXiv:1502.07144
prior_art.note: Catalytic colloids with broken action-reaction symmetry bond into molecules that oscillate or run and tumble. Particle-life's force matrix is an ad hoc version of the same physics.

prior_art.result: LITERATURE.md 2.4.1 and 2.8.1: active droplets and Gray-Scott spots have 'no heredity' because every body is one attractor
prior_art.nearest: Takagi & Kaneko, Differentiation and replication of spots in a reaction diffusion system with many chemicals, EPL (2001), arXiv nlin/0104058
prior_art.note: Random many-chemical networks give several spot types and multipotent spots that differentiate irreversibly. The work is 1D, with no lineage or selection measurement. The reference should cite it; the question is deferred.
